Welcome to the R Crash Course — part of a series of hands-on bioinformatics
training workshops. Each workshop is a self-contained, roughly two-hour
session; they don't depend on each other, so take them in whatever order
suits you.

## Workshops

### [Foundations of R with the Tidyverse](r_tidyverse_workshop.html)

Covers R basics (objects, data types, vectors) and the dplyr core verbs
(`filter`, `select`, `mutate`, `arrange`, `summarize`), group operations, and
a first `ggplot2` plot — using the built-in `starwars` dataset.

### [Metagenomics 1: Taxonomy and Function](metagenomics_taxonomy_function.html)

Covers what "-omics" means, amplicon vs. shotgun metagenomics, taxonomic and
functional annotation pipelines, diversity metrics, and choosing an approach
for a given research question.

### [Metagenomics 2: Viruses & Plasmids](metagenomics_viruses_plasmids.html)

Covers phage biology and applications, plasmid biology, and the specific
challenges of detecting viruses and mobile genetic elements in metagenomic
data.

### [RNA-seq and Transcriptomics](rnaseq_workshop.html)

Covers RNA-seq experimental design, the analysis workflow from raw reads to
a differential expression results table, and interpreting DESeq2 output.

### [Hot Topics in Bioinformatics](hot_topics_bioinformatics.html)

A tour of long-read sequencing, Nextflow, containers, reproducibility and
FAIR data, GitHub, and AI in bioinformatics (AlphaFold, LLMs, AI-assisted
coding).

### [Bioinformatics Tools: GitHub, HPC, and Cloud](bonus_bioinfo_tools.html)

A bonus session covering the infrastructure underneath most bioinformatics
work: version control with Git and GitHub, HPC cluster fundamentals, and
cloud computing.
